questions_visited.archetype: definition, projectile components, vertical velocity-time sketch and maximum-height calculation
questions_visited.why_selected: Provides an easy-to-medium connected projectile route with graph and sign decisions.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Define acceleration, split perpendicular motion, select a constant-acceleration equation and sketch signed velocity change.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Treat horizontal velocity as constant, treat vertical acceleration as downward, and use the top-of-path condition only for the vertical component.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Using one combined projectile velocity in a vertical equation or treating zero vertical velocity at maximum height as zero total velocity.
lesson_sections_informed: Choose the representation before the formula
Worked example: split a projectile before solving it
Correct mistakes by locating the first broken decision

questions_visited.archetype: constant deceleration using a no-time equation and velocity-time graph sketch in a mixed-topic context
questions_visited.why_selected: Shows that a Kinematics calculation can be isolated before later electric-field work.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Select v^2 = u^2 + 2as when time is absent and recognise a straight negative-gradient velocity-time graph.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Use initial velocity, final velocity and displacement with a declared sign convention, then represent constant acceleration by a straight graph.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Using a speed-only answer for a signed deceleration or introducing an unrelated electricity formula before completing the motion step.
lesson_sections_informed: Formula bank: use the condition as well as the symbols
Correct mistakes by locating the first broken decision

questions_visited.archetype: angled launch, resolved components, maximum height and resultant displacement
questions_visited.why_selected: Covers a multi-step projectile route that ends with displacement rather than travelled path length.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Resolve an initial velocity, use the vertical top condition, retain shared time, and combine perpendicular displacement components.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Solve vertical and horizontal motions separately, then use the two component displacements to find the resultant displacement.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Confusing the curved route with the straight-line displacement or using the launch speed instead of the vertical component at maximum height.
lesson_sections_informed: A dependable route through a kinematics question
Worked example: split a projectile before solving it

questions_visited.archetype: displacement definition, horizontal projection, vertical fall and resultant displacement
questions_visited.why_selected: Provides direct definition recall followed by a varied horizontal-projectile calculation.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: State precise displacement wording and use horizontal and vertical results in the correct roles.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Use constant horizontal velocity and vertical constant acceleration over the same flight time, then find the magnitude of the resultant displacement.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Calling horizontal distance the whole displacement or treating vertical distance as positive without declaring a direction.
lesson_sections_informed: A dependable route through a kinematics question
Worked example: split a projectile before solving it

questions_visited.archetype: acceleration definition, free-fall approximation and multi-stage light-gate timing
questions_visited.why_selected: Supplies the free-fall model condition and a harder stage-boundary calculation.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Justify negligible air resistance, select a constant-acceleration equation from rest and subtract two absolute times.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Model the dense ball as free fall, find each event time from the release, then subtract to obtain the interval.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Using diameter as the initial distance to the beam or treating the beam-block interval as a single fall from rest through the diameter.
lesson_sections_informed: Formula bank: use the condition as well as the symbols
Worked example: repair a free-fall setup
Correct mistakes by locating the first broken decision

questions_visited.archetype: velocity definition and vector resultant in a mixed-topic aircraft context
questions_visited.why_selected: Tests direction-aware velocity and the discipline of isolating a kinematics step in a larger question.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: State velocity precisely and combine directed velocity vectors before later-topic calculations.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Distinguish velocity from speed, retain directions, then add vectors by components or a correctly formed triangle.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Adding magnitudes without directions or allowing later energy and wave parts to obscure the initial motion decision.
lesson_sections_informed: A dependable route through a kinematics question
Correct mistakes by locating the first broken decision

questions_visited.archetype: velocity definition and constructed velocity-time graphs with changing gradient
questions_visited.why_selected: Provides an explicit graph-construction contrast between constant and decreasing acceleration.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Relate a graph's initial point, gradient, curvature and horizontal section to the motion description.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Start from rest, map constant acceleration to a straight line, then map decreasing acceleration to a curve whose gradient falls to zero.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Drawing a curve because velocity is increasing, rather than using curvature only when acceleration changes.
lesson_sections_informed: Choose the representation before the formula
